(1) PAB and GAb are highly specific serological markers for a subgroup (31%) of patients with Crohdn's disease and for a subgroup (29%) of patients with ulcerative Colitis; (2) PAB are not correlated with disease activity or treatment, whereas GAb are correlated with disease activity; (3) PAB are associated with pancreatic inflammation, but the relevance in the pathogenesis of Crohn's disease is unclear; (4) PAB and/or
the PAB were found to be a highly specific serologic marker for Crohn disease and the GAB a specific marker for ulcerative colitus.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a serological test for the diagnosis of Crohn's disease based on antibodies against pancreatic juice, which are highly specific and sensitive for this disease, but not for ulcerative colitits or other chronic inflammatory diseases.
the search for new markers for inflammatory bowel disease, which may be of diagnostic and pathogenic value.
the development and characterisation of two specific serological markers in Crohn's and ulcerative colitis.
